classification.difficultyReason: Use constant turnover to predict sales, reason about doubling price and sketch the contextual inverse-variation curve.

content.prompt: The owners of the Fizgig Manufacturing Company use a uniformly elastic demand curve to model their sales. Thus if the price of a Fizgig is $p$ and the quantity sold per year is $q$ then the turnover from sales is constant. That is, $pq=T$, for some constant $T$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Last year, the price of a Fizgig was $p=\$6$ and the quantity sold was $q=400\,000$. Find $T$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: The company’s board of directors want to raise the price to $p=\$8$ next year. How many Fizgigs can the company expect to sell if this happens?

children.label: c
children.prompt: Under this model, what will happen to the sales if the price is doubled instead?

answer.worked: Since $q=\frac{T}{p}$, replacing $p$ by $2p$ gives $q_{\text{new}}=\frac{T}{(2p)}=\frac{q}{2}$. Sales halve.

children.label: d
children.prompt: Sketch the graph of the demand curve with $q$ on the horizontal axis and $p$ on the vertical axis.

answer.short: $p=\dfrac{2\,400\,000}{q}$, $q>0$: a decreasing first-quadrant hyperbola with both axes as asymptotes.
answer.worked: Rearranging $pq=2\,400\,000$ gives $p=2\,400\,\frac{000}{q}$. Plot $(300\,000,8)$ and $(400\,000,6)$, then sketch the decreasing positive branch approaching both axes.

spec.description: Correct contextual demand curve; horizontal coordinate uses 1000 Fizgigs per drawing unit, with actual quantities printed.
spec.mathematics: p=2400000/q for q>0; passes through (300000,8) and (400000,6).
